intro: I took this to the room and brought in the Pixel-Art Sprite Animator, the Arcade Attract-Mode Showman, the Interface Motion Designer, the Low-Poly Retro Renderer from the studio roster. Here's where they agree, where they split, and what I'd do.

proposals.headline: Boot the cabinet from across the room — phosphor first, coin slot second.

moves.text: Frame 0–18 (0–300 ms): black screen flickers to CRT white scanline burst (full-width 1px horizontal sweep top-to-bottom over 8 frames), then snaps to dark background — phosphor-on entrance, ease-out, 60 fps on 1.
moves.where: 18 frames / CRT sweep / ease-out / frame 0

moves.text: Frame 18–60 (300–1000 ms): game title logotype slams in from top, 48px drop with 6-frame squash on land, overshoot +4px then settle — readable by frame 60, hierarchy locked.
moves.where: 42 frames / ease-out cubic / +4px overshoot / frame 18

moves.text: Frame 60–90 (1000–1500 ms): event details (date, venue) scroll up 32px from below, staggered 8 frames apart per line, ease-out — all text readable and settled by frame 90 (1.5 s deadline met).
moves.where: 30 frames / ease-out / 32px travel / staggered +8f each line

moves.text: Frame 90–132 (1500–2200 ms): PRESS START badge pulses in at 1 Hz blink cycle (30 frames on, 30 frames off), vector glow bloom radius 4px, integer-scaled pixel font only — entrance complete.
moves.where: 42 frames / 1 Hz / 30f on-30f off / bloom r=4px

moves.text: Idle loop from frame 132: scanline overlay drifts downward at 0.5px/frame, phosphor glow on logo breathes ±2px blur on a 120-frame linear sine — never stops, never repeats identically.
moves.where: 120-frame loop / linear / ±2px blur / 0.5px/f scanline drift

proposals.headline: Every pixel earns its place — silhouette and palette carry the whole entrance.

moves.text: Frame 0–12 (0–200 ms): 8-bit boot sprite (16×16 px, 4-colour palette) plays a 4-frame power-on animation at 12 fps (on 2s), integer-scaled 4× to 64px, nearest-neighbour only — no sub-pixel, no anti-alias.
moves.where: 12 frames / 12 fps on 2s / 4× integer scale / nearest-neighbour

moves.text: Frame 12–48 (200–800 ms): title text built from pixel font (8×8 grid, 2px letter-spacing) wipes left-to-right one character per 4 frames, palette cycles on highlight colour — readable, grid-locked, no rotation.
moves.where: 36 frames / 1 char per 4f / palette cycle on highlight

moves.text: Frame 48–72 (800–1200 ms): supporting info tiles drop in as 16×16 icon sprites (controller, star, coin), each 6-frame entrance cycle, strong silhouette key poses on frames 1 and 4 — no tweening between keys.
moves.where: 24 frames / 6-frame cycle / key poses f1+f4 / no tween

moves.text: Idle: character sprite on card corner runs a 6-frame walk cycle at 12 fps looping linear, moving 1px right per frame then wrapping — sub-pixel position held by colour shift, not coordinate float.
moves.where: 6-frame walk / 12 fps / linear / 1px/f / colour-shift sub-pixel

moves.text: Tilt response: parallax layers shift in integer-pixel steps only (±4px max per layer), nearest-neighbour, no interpolation — grid integrity absolute.
moves.where: ±4px / integer steps / nearest-neighbour / no lerp

proposals.headline: The card is a system — particle grid, audio-reactive, never the same loop twice.

moves.text: Entrance frame 0–132: a procedural particle grid (WebGL, 390px wide, 200 particles) spawns from centre outward over 80 frames using a seeded noise field — each run seeds differently, emergence is the effect.
moves.where: 80 frames / WebGL noise field / 200 particles / centre-out

moves.text: Text reveal driven by particle density threshold: when local particle density > 0.6 in a text-mask region, that glyph fades in (ease-out 12 frames) — hierarchy emerges from the system, not a keyframe.
moves.where: 12f per glyph / ease-out / density threshold 0.6 / mask-driven

moves.text: Idle loop: particle velocities respond to a 60 Hz audio-analysis bus (or simulated 120 BPM pulse if no mic); amplitude > 0.4 triggers velocity spike ×2.5, then exponential decay over 30 frames — alive, not baked.
moves.where: 30-frame decay / ×2.5 spike / 120 BPM pulse / linear decay

moves.text: RSVP yes: system rule inverts — particles collapse inward to a star-burst point in 20 frames (ease-in), hold 6 frames, then explode outward 40 frames (ease-out) — same rule, different parameter.
moves.where: 20f ease-in collapse / 6f hold / 40f ease-out burst / rule inversion

moves.text: Reduced-motion: system runs at 10% velocity cap, particles present but near-stationary — the rule still exists, the system is honest, nothing is faked.
moves.where: velocity cap 0.1× / particles visible / system intact / no fake

proposals.headline: The evite is a live signal — glitch is earned, not sprayed.

moves.text: Frame 0–6 (0–100 ms): raw RGB channel split (R +3px, B −3px horizontal offset) for 6 frames on entrance — real chromatic aberration math in WebGL fragment shader, not a preset filter.
moves.where: 6 frames / RGB split ±3px / WebGL frag shader / frame 0

moves.text: Frame 6–36 (100–600 ms): horizontal scanline dropout: 2–4 random lines per frame set to alpha 0 for 1 frame each, driven by Math.random() seeded to elapsed ms — imperfection is procedural, honest.
moves.where: 30 frames / 2–4 lines dropout / 1f duration / Math.random() seed

moves.text: Idle: low-level signal noise texture (8×8 grain tile, opacity 0.08) scrolls at 1px/frame diagonal — grain is structural, not decorative, matches 8.3 ms motion blur reference at 60 fps.
moves.where: continuous / 1px/f diagonal / opacity 0.08 / 8×8 tile

moves.text: Interactive beat moment: tap/click triggers a 4-frame full-card horizontal slice offset (slices 8px wide, alternating ±6px shift) then snaps back in 8 frames ease-in — feels like a signal hit, not a button.
moves.where: 4f slice offset ±6px / 8f ease-in snap / tap trigger / 8px slices

moves.text: Reduced-motion: dropout and grain remain at full opacity, channel split removed — texture stays honest, motion removed, signal body preserved.
moves.where: grain 0.08 / dropout retained / RGB split off / fallback

tensions: PIXEL_ART demands integer-pixel parallax steps (±4px, nearest-neighbour, no interpolation) to protect the grid; GENERATIVE insists the particle system must use floating-point positions and smooth density thresholds to let the system breathe — PIXEL_ART calls float positioning 'mixels on a phone screen at 390px', GENERATIVE calls integer-only 'baking a rule into a cage'.

ARCADE wants the PRESS START badge on a strict 1 Hz hardware-blink cycle (30 frames on, 30 off, no easing) because that is what pulled coins in 1983; UI_MOTION pushes back that a 1 Hz blink on a phone browser fails WCAG 2.3.1 (no flashing below 3 Hz threshold is safe) and demands the blink be replaced with a spring-physics pulse (stiffness 200, damping 20, 300 ms) that is interruptible and reduced-motion-aware — ARCADE calls it 'a slot machine with the lights off', UI_MOTION calls the raw blink 'an accessibility lawsuit waiting to load'.

plan.text: ENTRANCE — Frame 0–6: WebGL fragment shader fires a 6-frame RGB channel split (R +3px, B −3px) as the honest signal boot — earned glitch, not preset.
plan.where: 6 frames / ±3px RGB split / WebGL frag / ease-out / frame 0

plan.text: ENTRANCE — Frame 6–18: CRT scanline sweep (1px white horizontal line, top-to-bottom, 12 frames) snaps background into view — phosphor-on, 60 fps, linear.
ENTRANCE — Frame 18–60: title logotype drops 48px from above, ease-out cubic, 6-frame squash on land (+4px overshoot then settle) — readable and locked by frame 60 (1 s).
plan.where: 42 frames / ease-out cubic / 48px drop / +4px overshoot / squash 6f

plan.text: ENTRANCE — Frame 60–90: event detail lines scroll up 32px from below, staggered +8 frames per line, ease-out — all text readable by frame 90 (1.5 s, deadline met), 8.3 ms motion blur at 60 fps kept by 180° shutter rule.

IDLE LOOP — Frame 132+: PRESS START uses a spring-physics pulse (stiffness 200, damping 20, ~300 ms period) instead of raw 1 Hz blink — WCAG-safe, interruptible, still reads as arcade; scanline overlay drifts 0.5px/frame diagonal, grain tile (8×8, opacity 0.08) scrolls 1px/frame — system alive, never identical.
plan.where: 300 ms spring / stiffness 200 / damping 20 / 0.5px/f scanline / 1px/f grain

plan.text: TILT RESPONSE — Parallax layers shift in integer-pixel steps (±4px max, nearest-neighbour) for pixel-grid layers; WebGL particle layer shifts ±8px float — grid layers respect PIXEL_ART, generative layer gets its float, no mixels on the font.
plan.where: ±4px integer / nearest-neighbour for sprites / ±8px float for particles / pointer-driven

plan.text: INTERACTIVE MOMENT — Tap triggers playable beat: 4-frame horizontal slice glitch (8px slices, ±6px alternating shift, ease-in snap back over 8 frames), then a 6-frame pixel-sprite drum hit animation (integer-scaled 4×, 12 fps) plays on a 120 BPM grid — player taps in rhythm, card responds, feels played not pressed.
plan.where: 4f glitch / 8px slices / 8f snap / 6-frame sprite / 12 fps / 120 BPM

plan.text: RSVP YES — Particle system collapses inward (ease-in 20 frames), holds 6 frames, explodes outward (ease-out 40 frames) with palette-cycle colour burst — same generative rule, inverted parameters, celebration is the system answering; REDUCED MOTION VERSION: RGB split and scanline sweep removed, title fades in over 18 frames (opacity 0→1, ease-out), PRESS START spring-pulse retained at 50% amplitude, grain and particle system run at 10% velocity — finished, honest, not stripped bare.
plan.where: 20f ease-in / 6f hold / 40f ease-out / reduced: 18f fade / 50% pulse / 0.1× velocity

summary: The card boots like a cabinet: a 6-frame earned RGB-split signals the power-on, a 12-frame scanline sweep lights the field, and the title lands with weight and squash by 1 second — all text readable by 1.5 s, 180° shutter motion blur honoured throughout. The idle is a live system: spring-pulsing PRESS START (WCAG-safe, interruptible), drifting scanlines and grain that never loop identically. Parallax respects both camps — pixel layers step in integers, the WebGL particle field floats. The interactive beat plays the card like an instrument at 120 BPM, rewarded with a slice-glitch hit and a sprite drum frame. RSVP yes inverts the generative rule into a collapse-and-burst. Reduced motion strips only movement, never finish: the system breathes slowly, the grain stays honest, the card still looks complete.
